large_guidance: The heavy op in GPT-2 is the Linear (matmul) layers — specifically `Conv1D` modules in HuggingFace GPT-2 (which are `y = x @ W + b` with `W` of shape `[in_features, out_features]`), plus the final `lm_head` Linear that projects hidden states to vocab logits (768 -> 50257). These matmuls dominate runtime and were never replaced — your previous attempt only fused LayerNorm and GELU. You MUST replace these matmuls with a custom Triton GEMM kernel that executes unconditionally on the forward path. Concretely: (1) Write a tiled Triton GEMM kernel `matmul_kernel(A, B, C, bias, M, N, K, stride_am, stride_ak, stride_bk, stride_bn, stride_cm, stride_cn, BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K, GROUP_M)` that computes `C = A @ B (+ bias)` using `tl.dot` with `BLOCK_M=64/128, BLOCK_N=64/128, BLOCK_K=32/64`, accumulator in fp32, grouped program-id swizzling for L2 reuse, and an optional add-bias epilogue. Reshape the 3D input `[B, S, K]` to `[B*S, K]` before launch. Note GPT-2's `Conv1D` stores weight as `[in, out]` (no transpose needed) — handle this layout directly. (2) Create a `TritonLinear` nn.Module that holds `weight` and `bias` references from the original module and calls your matmul kernel in `forward`; then walk `self.model` and replace EVERY `transformers.pytorch_utils.Conv1D` instance (these implement qkv projection, attention output projection, MLP fc, MLP proj) AND the final `nn.Linear` lm_head with `TritonLinear`. Use `isinstance` against the imported `Conv1D` class, or match by class name string `"Conv1D"`. Do NOT wrap with any `if self.training` / `if x.is_cuda` guard — call the Triton kernel unconditionally. (3) For correctness, ensure dtype handling matches (cast inputs to fp32 if weights are fp32), contiguous-ify A before launch, and verify output shape exactly matches `x @ W + b` of the reference. Do not pre-reduce or fold any axis of W or x; the kernel must perform the full M*N*K multiply-adds. After this replacement, the runtime verifier will see the heavy op executed in Triton, not PyTorch.
